page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.e4.xlarge is an x86_64 architecture virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 4 shared vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores using an Intel Xeon E5-2682 v4 processor operating at 2.5 GHz. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates that the ecs.e4.xlarge delivers modest performance characteristics. In stress-ng testing, single-core CPU performance scored 950.58, placing it in the bottom 10%, while multi-core performance reached 3679.45, placing it in the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth tests show 321.53 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 30.12 GB/sec for uncached large blocks, both falling into the bottom 25%. Database and key-value operations, such as Redis SET, achieved 5.32 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput reached 4.72 GB/sec.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.e4.xlarge lies in its shared CPU allocation and older Intel Xeon architecture, which limits raw compute throughput but provides a high memory density of 32.0 GB. This makes the instance a qualitatively cost-efficient option for memory-intensive workloads that do not require sustained high CPU performance. It is suited for lightweight database operations, caching layers, static web serving, and basic memory-heavy background tasks rather than intensive computational or real-time processing workloads.
